record.context_brief: Monochromatic cycle partitions in mean colourings
record.original_question: For each r, does there exist a constant m(r) such that the vertex set of any r-mean edge-coloured graph can be partitioned into at most m(r) monochromatic cycles?

evidence.quote: Question 8.3. Does there exist a constant m(r), depending only on r, such that the vertex set of any r-mean coloured graph may be partitioned into at most m(r) cycles?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a (finite, simple) graph and let c:E→ℕ be an edge colouring. For a vertex v∈V, write d_c(v) for the number of distinct colours appearing on edges incident to v. The colouring c is called r-mean if 

  (1/|V|) · Σ_{v∈V} d_c(v) ≤ r,

i.e. the average over vertices of the number of colours seen at a vertex is at most r. A monochromatic cycle is a cycle (in the graph-theoretic sense, where single vertices and single edges are also permitted as degenerate cycles) all of whose edges have the same colour.

Question. For every positive integer r, does there exist a constant m(r), depending only on r, with the following property: for every graph G and every r-mean edge colouring of G, the vertex set V(G) can be partitioned into at most m(r) sets, each of which induces a monochromatic cycle?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up substantial work on monochromatic cycle partitions for r-edge-coloured and r-locally coloured complete graphs (Conlon–Stein, Sárközy, Letzter–Pokrovskiy, and others), but no source claims a resolution for the more general r-mean coloured setting. The mean-colouring variant appears to remain open as of recent literature (2024–2026).

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic cycle partitions in local edge colourings
status_evidence.snippet: For any natural number r, the vertex set of any r-locally coloured complete graph may be partitioned into O(r^2 log r) disjoint monochromatic cycles.
status_evidence.claim: Results are known for r-local colourings of complete graphs, but not for the weaker r-mean condition on general graphs.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic cycle partitions of r-edge-coloured graphs with high minimum degree
status_evidence.snippet: How many vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles are needed to cover the vertex set of an r-edge-coloured graph as a function of its minimum degree.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats r-edge colourings under minimum-degree assumptions, not the r-mean setting of the question.
